# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Plock_2017_TAK648_mouse"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Plock_2017_TAK648_mouse"))$description`
* Article (open access): <https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.12436>

TAK-648 is a selective phosphodiesterase-4 (PDE4) inhibitor developed for type
2 diabetes. Plock et al. compared it head-to-head with roflumilast and
roflumilast N-oxide in db/db mice, related the HbA1c time course to an exposure
surrogate (total PDE4 inhibition, tPDE4i), and translated the mouse result to a
human efficacious dose using roflumilast's clinical tPDE4i as the bridge. This
vignette reproduces the mouse PK/PD model and the translation arithmetic.

# Population

Female leptin-receptor-deficient db/db mice (BKS.Cg-m+/+Lepr db/BomTac), 7
weeks old at the start of treatment, received once-daily oral gavage for 28
days. Eight PD groups of 10 animals each (vehicle; TAK-648 1, 3, 10 mg/kg;
roflumilast 0.3, 1, 3 mg/kg; roflumilast N-oxide 3 mg/kg) had HbA1c measured on
study days -1, 14 and 28 and two sparse PK samples each. Three satellite PK
groups of 6 animals provided richer PK sampling (Supplementary Methods and
Supplementary Table 1). The PK/PD model was fitted to the 80 PD animals.

The same information is available from the model's `population` metadata
(`readModelDb("Plock_2017_TAK648_mouse")()$population`).

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| HbA1c = H0 + SLOPE * (1 - EMAX * tPDE4i / (PDE50 + tPDE4i)) * DAY | -- | Eq. 4; Supplementary PK/PD model code (`$PRED`) |
| AUC = F * Dose / CL (F = 1) | -- | Eq. 2; Results ("Bioavailability was fixed to a typical value of 100%") |
| tPDE4i = AUC * fu / (IC50 * tau), summed over roflumilast + N-oxide | -- | Eq. 3 and following text |
| `lrbase` (H0) | 4.35 % | Table 2 |
| `lslope` (SLOPE) | 0.138 %/day | Table 2 |
| `lemax` (EMAX) | 1.00 | Table 2 |
| `lec50_tak648` (PDE50, TAK-648) | 1.10 | Table 2 |
| `lec50_roflumilast` (PDE50, roflumilast(-N-oxide)) | 27.1 | Table 2 |
| `etalrbase` | 12.7 CV% | Table 2 BSV_H0 |
| `etalslope` | 21.4 CV% | Table 2 BSV_slope |
| `etalec50` (shared by both PDE50) | 79.8 CV% | Table 2 BSV_PDE50; `ETA(3)` on both PDE50 lines of the `$PRED` |
| `propSd` | 3.87 CV% | Table 2 residual variability; `Y=A1C+A1C*EPS(1)` |
| `lcl_tak648` | 2.97 L/h/kg | Results, "TAK-648 pharmacokinetic" |
| `lcl_roflumilast`, `lcl_noxide` (roflumilast dosing) | 2.34, 3.52 L/h/kg | Results, "Pharmacokinetic of roflumilast and roflumilast-N-oxide" |
| `lcl_roflumilast_noxidedose`, `lcl_noxide_noxidedose` (N-oxide dosing) | 41.8, 1.09 L/h/kg | Same paragraph |
| `fu_*` (TAK-648, roflumilast, N-oxide) | 0.200, 0.037, 0.127 | Paragraph below Table 1 |
| `ic50_*` (TAK-648, roflumilast, N-oxide) | 5.77, 0.282, 0.629 ug/L | Paragraph below Table 1 |
| `tau` | 24 h | Once-daily dosing (Methods) |

# Exposure link: tPDE4i against Table 1

The model rebuilds each animal's exposure from its daily dose with the typical
apparent clearances. Table 1 of the paper lists the geometric mean of the
individual (post hoc) AUC and tPDE4i values of the PD animals, so agreement is
expected to within a few percent, not exactly.

```{r exposure}
mod <- readModelDb("Plock_2017_TAK648_mouse")
p <- rxode2::rxode(mod)$theta

arms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,                    ~DOSE_TAK648_MGKG, ~DOSE_ROFLUMILAST_MGKG, ~DOSE_ROFLUMILASTNOXIDE_MGKG, ~tpde4i_table1,
  "Vehicle",                0,                 0,                      0,                             0,
  "TAK-648 1 mg/kg",        1,                 0,                      0,                             0.486,
  "TAK-648 3 mg/kg",        3,                 0,                      0,                             1.41,
  "TAK-648 10 mg/kg",       10,                0,                      0,                             4.70,
  "Roflumilast 0.3 mg/kg",  0,                 0.3,                    0,                             1.49,
  "Roflumilast 1 mg/kg",    0,                 1,                      0,                             4.55,
  "Roflumilast 3 mg/kg",    0,                 3,                      0,                             13.8,
  "N-oxide 3 mg/kg",        0,                 0,                      3,                             22.5
)
arms$arm <- factor(arms$arm, levels = arms$arm)

tp <- function(auc, fu, ic50) auc * fu / (ic50 * p[["tau"]])
exposure <- arms |>
  mutate(
    auc_tak = 1000 * DOSE_TAK648_MGKG / exp(p[["lcl_tak648"]]),
    auc_rof = 1000 * DOSE_ROFLUMILAST_MGKG / exp(p[["lcl_roflumilast"]]) +
      1000 * DOSE_ROFLUMILASTNOXIDE_MGKG / exp(p[["lcl_roflumilast_noxidedose"]]),
    auc_nox = 1000 * DOSE_ROFLUMILAST_MGKG / exp(p[["lcl_noxide"]]) +
      1000 * DOSE_ROFLUMILASTNOXIDE_MGKG / exp(p[["lcl_noxide_noxidedose"]]),
    tpde4i_model = tp(auc_tak, p[["fu_tak648"]], p[["ic50_tak648"]]) +
      tp(auc_rof, p[["fu_roflumilast"]], p[["ic50_roflumilast"]]) +
      tp(auc_nox, p[["fu_noxide"]], p[["ic50_noxide"]]),
    pct_diff = 100 * (tpde4i_model / tpde4i_table1 - 1)
  )

exposure |>
  filter(arm != "Vehicle") |>
  select(arm, tpde4i_model, tpde4i_table1, pct_diff) |>
  rename(
    "Treatment" = arm,
    "tPDE4i (model, typical)" = tpde4i_model,
    "tPDE4i (Table 1, geometric mean)" = tpde4i_table1,
    "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = c(0, 3, 3, 1))

stopifnot(all(abs(exposure$pct_diff[-1]) < 6))
```

The TAK-648 1 mg/kg row reproduces Table 1 exactly (1000 / 2.97 = 337 ug*h/L,
tPDE4i 0.486), which also confirms that the printed clearances are per kg.

# Typical HbA1c trajectories: Figure 2

The model is algebraic in time, so a typical-value solve can be checked against
the closed form directly, and then against the median lines of the paper's
visual predictive check. The median and 90% prediction-interval lines of Figure
2 were digitised by the maintainers from the published raster at study day 8
(day 20 for the 10 mg/kg TAK-648 panel, whose lines overlap the observations at
day 8).

```{r typical}
times <- c(0, 8, 14, 20, 28)
ev_typ <- arms |>
  mutate(id = seq_len(n())) |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = times) |>
  mutate(evid = 0, amt = 0) |>
  as.data.frame()

mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = ev_typ, keep = "arm") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(arm = factor(arm, levels = levels(arms$arm)))

# Closed form of Eq. 4 with the typical values
closed <- typ |>
  left_join(select(exposure, arm, tpde4i_model), by = "arm") |>
  mutate(
    pde50 = ifelse(grepl("TAK", arm), exp(p[["lec50_tak648"]]), exp(p[["lec50_roflumilast"]])),
    eff = exp(p[["lemax"]]) * tpde4i_model / (pde50 + tpde4i_model),
    hba1c_closed = exp(p[["lrbase"]]) + exp(p[["lslope"]]) * (1 - eff) * time
  )
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(closed$Hba1c, closed$hba1c_closed, tolerance = 1e-8)))

# Digitised Figure 2 lines (5th percentile, median, 95th percentile).
# Panels b-d are TAK-648 and e-g roflumilast; see "Assumptions and deviations".
fig2 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,                    ~panel, ~day, ~p05, ~p50, ~p95,
  "Vehicle",               "a",    8,    4.44, 5.47, 6.65,
  "TAK-648 1 mg/kg",       "b",    8,    4.12, 5.06, 6.29,
  "TAK-648 3 mg/kg",       "c",    8,    3.88, 4.85, 6.06,
  "TAK-648 10 mg/kg",      "d",    20,   3.91, 4.94, 6.32,
  "Roflumilast 0.3 mg/kg", "e",    8,    4.41, 5.35, 6.59,
  "Roflumilast 1 mg/kg",   "f",    8,    4.32, 5.29, 6.50,
  "Roflumilast 3 mg/kg",   "g",    8,    4.12, 5.09, 6.29,
  "N-oxide 3 mg/kg",       "h",    8,    4.00, 4.97, 6.12
) |>
  mutate(arm = factor(arm, levels = levels(arms$arm)))

cmp_median <- fig2 |>
  left_join(select(typ, arm, time, Hba1c), by = c("arm", "day" = "time")) |>
  mutate(diff = Hba1c - p50)

cmp_median |>
  select(arm, panel, day, p50, Hba1c, diff) |>
  rename(
    "Treatment" = arm, "Figure 2 panel" = panel, "Day" = day,
    "Figure 2 median (%)" = p50, "Model typical (%)" = Hba1c,
    "Difference (% HbA1c)" = diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

stopifnot(all(abs(cmp_median$diff) < 0.12))
```

```{r typical-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
ggplot(typ, aes(time, Hba1c, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = cmp_median, aes(day, p50, colour = arm), shape = 4, size = 3) +
  labs(
    x = "Time since pre-treatment HbA1c (day)", y = "HbA1c (%)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Lines: model typical values. Crosses: digitised medians of Plock 2017 Figure 2."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

# Visual predictive check: Figure 2 prediction intervals

A stochastic simulation with 200 animals per arm draws the three random effects
and the proportional residual error. Unlike the published check, it uses each
arm's typical tPDE4i rather than every animal's individual value; the
individual tPDE4i spread in Table 1 (68% range within about +/-15%) is small
beside the 79.8% CV of PDE50.

```{r vpc, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20170111)
n_per_arm <- 200
ev_sto <- arms |>
  tidyr::crossing(rep = seq_len(n_per_arm)) |>
  mutate(id = seq_len(n())) |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = seq(0, 28, by = 2)) |>
  mutate(evid = 0, amt = 0) |>
  as.data.frame()

sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_sto, keep = "arm") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(arm = factor(arm, levels = levels(arms$arm)))

vpc <- sim |>
  group_by(arm, time) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(sim, 0.05), p50 = median(sim), p95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(vpc, aes(time)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50)) +
  geom_point(
    data = tidyr::pivot_longer(fig2, c(p05, p50, p95), values_to = "HbA1c"),
    aes(day, HbA1c), colour = "red", shape = 4, size = 2.5
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~arm, ncol = 4) +
  labs(
    x = "Time since pre-treatment HbA1c (day)", y = "HbA1c (%)",
    caption = paste(
      "Grey band: simulated 90% prediction interval; line: simulated median.",
      "Red crosses: digitised Plock 2017 Figure 2 lines."
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw()

cmp_pi <- fig2 |>
  left_join(vpc, by = c("arm", "day" = "time"), suffix = c("_fig", "_sim")) |>
  mutate(d05 = p05_sim - p05_fig, d50 = p50_sim - p50_fig, d95 = p95_sim - p95_fig)

cmp_pi |>
  select(arm, day, p05_fig, p05_sim, p50_fig, p50_sim, p95_fig, p95_sim) |>
  rename(
    "Treatment" = arm, "Day" = day,
    "P5 Figure 2" = p05_fig, "P5 sim" = p05_sim,
    "Median Figure 2" = p50_fig, "Median sim" = p50_sim,
    "P95 Figure 2" = p95_fig, "P95 sim" = p95_sim
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

# Centre and robust spread, not single-cohort extremes: the median offset over
# the eight arms catches a transposed parameter or an omega read as its square
# root, and the per-arm bound allows for sampling noise in a 200-animal
# percentile (standard error about 0.08 % HbA1c). With 400,000 animals per arm
# the expected offsets are +0.03 (P5), -0.01 (median) and -0.06 (P95).
stopifnot(
  abs(median(cmp_pi$d50)) < 0.1,
  abs(median(cmp_pi$d05)) < 0.25,
  abs(median(cmp_pi$d95)) < 0.25,
  all(abs(c(cmp_pi$d05, cmp_pi$d95)) < 0.5)
)
```

# Half-maximal doses in db/db mice

The paper states that the half-maximal effect would be reached with 2.3 mg/kg
TAK-648 and 5.9 mg/kg roflumilast. With tPDE4i linear in dose, the dose that
gives tPDE4i = PDE50 is PDE50 divided by the tPDE4i per mg/kg.

```{r ed50}
tp_per_mgkg <- exposure |>
  filter(arm %in% c("TAK-648 1 mg/kg", "Roflumilast 1 mg/kg")) |>
  pull(tpde4i_model)
ed50 <- tibble::tibble(
  Compound = c("TAK-648", "Roflumilast"),
  `Model (mg/kg)` = c(exp(p[["lec50_tak648"]]), exp(p[["lec50_roflumilast"]])) / tp_per_mgkg,
  `Plock 2017 (mg/kg)` = c(2.3, 5.9)
) |>
  mutate(`Difference (%)` = 100 * (`Model (mg/kg)` / `Plock 2017 (mg/kg)` - 1))
knitr::kable(ed50, digits = 2)
stopifnot(all(abs(ed50$`Difference (%)`) < 5))
```

The roflumilast value is 3% lower than printed because the paper scaled the
Table 1 geometric-mean tPDE4i (4.55 per mg/kg gives 27.1 / 4.55 = 5.96 mg/kg),
while the model uses the typical clearances (4.73 per mg/kg).

# Human dose translation

Eq. 5 carries the TAK-648 to roflumilast potency ratio from mice to humans, using
the clinical tPDE4i of 1.03 for 500 ug roflumilast (cited by the paper from its
reference 12). Eq. 6 converts the required tPDE4i to a plasma AUC with the human
unbound fraction 0.667. The paper reports a required AUC of 8.74 ug*h/L and a
therapeutic dose of 100 ug.

```{r human}
tpde4i_rof_human <- 1.03 # Plock 2017 Methods, Eq. 5 text
fu_tak648_human <- 0.667 # Plock 2017 Results, 'Prediction of therapeutic exposure in humans'
tpde4i_req <- exp(p[["lec50_tak648"]]) * tpde4i_rof_human / exp(p[["lec50_roflumilast"]])
auc_req <- tpde4i_req * p[["ic50_tak648"]] * p[["tau"]] / fu_tak648_human
c(required_tPDE4i = tpde4i_req, required_AUC = auc_req, published_AUC = 8.74)
stopifnot(abs(auc_req / 8.74 - 1) < 0.02)

# First-in-human dose-normalised AUCinf (Plock 2017 Table 4, means)
fih <- tibble::tibble(
  dose_mg = c(0.05, 0.15, 0.35, 0.7, 0.85),
  aucinf = c(4.58, 16.81, 28.27, 75.77, 93.84)
) |>
  mutate(dose_for_target_ug = 1000 * dose_mg * 8.74 / aucinf)
fih |>
  rename(
    "FIH dose (mg)" = dose_mg, "Mean AUCinf (ug*h/L)" = aucinf,
    "Dose giving AUC 8.74 (ug)" = dose_for_target_ug
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
stopifnot(abs(median(fih$dose_for_target_ug) / 100 - 1) < 0.25)
```

Each first-in-human cohort's dose-normalised exposure puts the target AUC at
about 80-110 ug, which the paper rounds to a predicted therapeutic dose of 100
ug (0.1 mg) daily. The paper does not say which cohorts it pooled, so only the
order of magnitude is checked here.

# Non-compartmental analysis

No PKNCA analysis is run. The packaged model has no concentration-time output:
the mouse PK enters only through steady-state AUC = Dose / CL, checked against
Table 1 above, and the human first-in-human data (Table 4) are a separate NCA
with no population model in the paper.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Figure 2 panel labels.** The caption lists panels (b)-(d) as roflumilast
  0.3/1/3 mg/kg, (e) as roflumilast N-oxide and (f)-(h) as TAK-648 1/3/10 mg/kg.
  The plotted medians match the model only in the order of Supplementary Table 1:
  (a) vehicle, (b)-(d) TAK-648 1/3/10 mg/kg, (e)-(g) roflumilast 0.3/1/3 mg/kg,
  (h) roflumilast N-oxide. Under the caption's order the 3 mg/kg roflumilast arm
  (tPDE4i 13.8, typical day-28 HbA1c 6.9%) would be panel (d), whose median ends
  near 5.2%; under the Supplementary Table 1 order every panel agrees to within
  0.07 % HbA1c. The comparisons above use the Supplementary Table 1 order.
* **Time axis.** The paper defines study day -1 as DAY = 0, and Figure 2 plots
  the HbA1c samples at 0, 14 and 28. The model's time is days since the
  pre-treatment measurement, with the drug effect acting from time 0, as in
  Eq. 4.
* **Exposure from dose.** The published `$PRED` reads each animal's tPDE4i from
  the dataset, derived from its post hoc CL and F. The individual PK random
  effects are not reported (only the 19% CV on TAK-648 F), so the model computes
  a typical tPDE4i from the daily dose. Users with individual exposures can
  reproduce the paper's input by adjusting the dose covariate in proportion.
* **Clearance units.** The Results print the clearances as L/h; Eq. 2 and the
  Table 1 AUC values (1000 / 2.97 = 337 ug*h/L for 1 mg/kg) show they are
  L/h/kg.
* **Mouse compartmental PK not packaged.** The TAK-648 one-compartment model
  (dose-group-specific and day-1-specific absorption, day-1-specific clearance)
  and the roflumilast / N-oxide two-compartment models report only apparent
  clearances and the steady-state absorption half-lives of TAK-648 (74, 85 and
  168 min); no volumes or roflumilast absorption rates are printed, so no
  concentration-time model can be built. The PD model needs only the
  steady-state AUC, which the clearances fully determine.
* **Mixtures.** Every animal received a single compound. The model writes Eq. 4
  through the potency-normalised exposure x = tPDE4i(TAK-648) / PDE50(TAK-648)
  + tPDE4i(roflumilast) / PDE50(roflumilast), which equals the published
  EMAX * CE / (PDE50 + CE) for any single compound. Behaviour for a mixture of
  TAK-648 and roflumilast is an additive extension that the paper did not test.
* **IIV scale.** Table 2 reports the between-animal variability as CV%; the
  variances are taken as omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2). The alternative reading
  omega^2 = CV^2 changes the simulated 90% intervals by at most about 0.1 %
  HbA1c at day 28, and the median offset from the digitised Figure 2 lines by
  about 0.01 % HbA1c at the comparison days, which is below what a 1-pixel
  (0.06 % HbA1c) digitisation can resolve.
* **Human translation constants.** The roflumilast clinical tPDE4i of 1.03 and
  the human TAK-648 unbound fraction of 0.667 are human-side constants used only
  in the translation section; they are not model parameters.
* **Errata.** A search of Europe PMC on 2026-11-25 found no erratum or
  correction for this article.
